notes: Trade is in gross weight (kt), mostly HS 8105 (mattes, intermediate products such as crude hydroxide, unwrought cobalt, scrap and powders): ores and concentrates (HS 2605) are only 8 kt of the 743 kt (1%) that the HS4 extract gives for both headings in 2024, before the cleaning rules. USGS production is contained cobalt (t Co), so the two are not comparable.

DR Congo to China is the main flow (629 kt, declared at 4,805 USD per tonne, against 17,957 USD per tonne for all other flows): by its unit value it is mostly intermediate products rather than metal; customs data do not say so.

DR Congo suspended its cobalt exports until 15 October 2025 and, from 16 October 2025, caps them by quota: 18,125 t for the rest of 2025 and 96,600 t a year for 2026 and 2027, set by its regulator ARECOMS (https://source.benchmarkminerals.com/article/drc-to-lift-cobalt-export-ban-and-impose-quotas-through-2027). The 2024 flows shown here predate these measures; the basis of the quotas (contained or gross weight) is not compared with the tables.
